why: Building the string greedily by always placing the most frequent remaining letter (other than the one just placed) is the classic max-heap pattern; holding the last letter out of the heap for one step enforces the no-adjacent rule.
hints: If one letter appears more than ceil(n/2) times, no arrangement exists. Otherwise, what should go next?
Always place the eligible letter with the most copies left (ties: smallest letter), where the letter just placed is not eligible.
Max-heap of (-count, letter). Pop the best, append it, push back the letter held from the previous step, then hold this one if copies remain. O(n log 26).
pitfalls: The tie rule is part of the judged answer: equal counts go to the lexicographically smaller letter.
Push the previously held letter back after popping, not before, or it may be picked twice in a row.
Return "" when impossible (check max count > (n + 1) // 2 up front).
